requirement_text.REQ-033:
FIRST REQUIREMENT OF RELEASE 2 (PRD 4's "next Fail Stories, Q4 - 7 stories", PRD 14 build-order step 7). Release 2 covers exactly seven stories: B6, B7, B8, B9, F3, F4, F9. This requirement is the schema enabler all of B7/B8/F4/F9 need and none of them can create for itself without three requirements racing to define the same table.

It follows the REQ-010/REQ-011/REQ-025/REQ-031 precedent exactly: schema-bearing work is drafted as its own DATA-DESIGNER-owned requirement producing a design artefact under docs/agents/design/ PLUS the migration under apps/bot/, so DATA-DESIGNER's step is separable from the BACKEND-DEV requirements that consume it. (REQ-010 and REQ-011 are owner: DATA-DESIGNER; REQ-025 and REQ-031 are owner: BACKEND-DEV and carry their schema inline because their table exists only to serve one flow. InviteCode serves four separate flows, so it takes REQ-010's shape, not REQ-025's.)

VERIFIED CURRENT STATE (read from apps/bot/src/db/schema.ts at drafting time -- re-verify before changing, per HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md 1.1, do not trust this paragraph): there is NO InviteCode table anywhere in the schema. The `registrations` table carries `inviteCodeId: uuid("invite_code_id")` as a PLAIN UUID COLUMN WITH NO FOREIGN KEY, and the comment above it reads: "No FK: no InviteCode table exists in this requirement's scope (REQ-011.md 11 open question 3). A future requirement adds the FK." THIS IS THAT REQUIREMENT. Adding the FK is not scope creep; it is the deferred half of an explicitly-recorded open question being closed at the point the referenced table finally exists.

Scope of work -- one entity plus one FK plus one generator:
- InviteCode, per PRD 5: event_id - code(UNIQUE) - issued_to_user_id(nullable) - grants_companion_of(user_id, nullable) - max_uses - used_count - expires_at. UUID primary key and created/updated timestamps like every other entity (PRD 5 preamble).
- The three code SHAPES PRD FR-5 and story F4 name are COMPOSITIONS of those columns, not a fourth `type` enum column: PERSONAL is issued_to_user_id non-null with max_uses=1; BULK is issued_to_user_id null with max_uses=N; COMPANION is grants_companion_of non-null. The design artefact states this composition explicitly and states which combinations are legal, because REQ-037 (issuing) and REQ-038/REQ-039 (redeeming) all branch on it and must not each invent their own reading. This mirrors DESIGN-REVIEW.md's own reasoning for requires_invite/requires_approval being two booleans rather than one access enum ("compositions, not special cases").
- The FK: registrations.invite_code_id becomes a real foreign key to invite_codes.id, replacing the plain uuid column, with the same onDelete posture as the other person/event references in that table (`restrict` -- a redeemed code is history and must not be deletable out from under a registration; the design artefact states this).
- The code VALUE generator: security-invariants.md S4 sets the SAME bar for InviteCode values as for qr_token -- cryptographically secure source, never Math.random, never a sequential id, never a hash of a user id. It must also be human-typeable, because story B7 requires redemption "by typing it" as well as by `?start=i_<code>` deep link. These two pull against each other and the design artefact must resolve the tension explicitly (an alphabet excluding visually ambiguous characters, with a stated length giving the entropy S4 demands). apps/bot/src/domain/registration.ts's generateQrToken() is the existing CSPRNG precedent to follow, not to copy verbatim -- its 64-character hex output is not typeable.
- used_count is a STORED counter and this is NOT a violation of PRD 5's computed-never-stored rule. PRD 5 names exactly five computed values (no_show, waitlist position, seats taken, registration_open, finished) and lists `used_count` as an InviteCode FIELD in the same block. Stated here because a reader who has internalized REQ-017/REQ-021's discipline will otherwise flag it. It is nonetheless subject to S7-style atomicity at increment time, which is REQ-038's problem, not this one's.
- NO handlers, NO domain logic, NO issuing or redemption flow -- REQ-037 and REQ-038 own those. This requirement produces the design artefact and the migration only, exactly as REQ-010 and REQ-011 did.

OPEN QUESTION, flagged rather than silently resolved (docs/agents/decisions/ is the place it would be settled if it needs to be): PRD FR-4's row `requires_invite=true, requires_approval=false` states "Valid code -> admitted; no code -> offer wishlist", and FR-4 additionally says "A user who has checked_in_at on any past event satisfies requires_invite without a code (eligibility rule, CONFIGURABLE PER EVENT)". "Configurable per event" implies an Event-level flag that PRD 5's Event entity does not list. This requirement does NOT add such a column -- inventing an unlisted Event field is exactly what PRD's closing rule forbids, and REQ-026's doors-time episode is this registry's own precedent for reading an existing field rather than adding one. REQ-038 owns the eligibility rule and must state how it resolves "configurable per event" (a new flag needing a decision record, or the rule applying uniformly to every requires_invite event); this requirement records the question so REQ-038 cannot inherit it silently.

task.description: WF-02 Step 1 (Design) for REQ-033, on branch feature/WF02-REQ-033. Verify branch first (git branch --show-current must equal feature/WF02-REQ-033). Produce docs/agents/design/REQ-033.md: the InviteCode table shape, the registrations.invite_code_id FK closure, and the CSPRNG+typeable code-generator design. This requirement is DATA-DESIGNER-owned (schema-bearing, serves four downstream flows: REQ-037 issuing, REQ-038 redemption, REQ-039 companion, REQ-040 invitation list) per the REQ-010/REQ-011 precedent. Design artefact only -- no migration file, no handler code, no domain logic in this step (that is BACKEND-DEV's Step 2, next).
acceptance_criteria: The migration creates an invite_codes table with a UUID primary key, created/updated timestamps, and columns for event_id, code, issued_to_user_id, grants_companion_of, max_uses, used_count and expires_at -- verified by applying the migration to a scratch Postgres database and pasting the resulting schema into the verification report (PRD 5).

invite_codes.code carries a UNIQUE constraint that is actually enforced: verified by inserting the same code value twice against the scratch database and confirming the second insert fails with a unique-violation error. Reading the schema is not sufficient; the duplicate insert must be attempted.

invite_codes.issued_to_user_id and invite_codes.grants_companion_of are both nullable and both reference users.id, verified by inserting a bulk code supplying neither (must succeed) and a code whose issued_to_user_id names a non-existent user id (must fail on the foreign key) -- both cases run (PRD 5).

registrations.invite_code_id is a real FOREIGN KEY to invite_codes.id after this migration, verified by attempting to insert a registration whose invite_code_id names a non-existent invite_codes row and confirming it FAILS -- an insert that succeeds proves the FK was not added and is a FAIL of this criterion (REQ-011.md 11 open question 3, closed here).

Deleting an invite_codes row that a registration references is refused by the database, verified by constructing exactly that pair and attempting the delete (the restrict posture this requirement's design states).

The code generator draws from a cryptographically secure source: verified by reading the generation code (it must call crypto.randomBytes or an equivalent CSPRNG -- a git grep for Math.random in the generator's module must return no hit) AND by generating 10000 codes in a test and asserting zero collisions (security-invariants.md S4).

The generated code contains only characters from the design artefact's stated typeable alphabet, and the artefact states the resulting entropy in bits with the arithmetic shown -- verified by generating 1000 codes, asserting every character is in the alphabet, and reading the artefact's entropy calculation (S4 plus story B7's 'or by typing it').

The design artefact under docs/agents/design/ states: how personal, bulk and companion codes are composed from the columns (not a type enum); which column combinations are legal; and the FR-4 'configurable per event' eligibility open question as an unresolved question routed to REQ-038, not a decision made here.
No column named no_show, waitlist_position, seats_taken, registration_open or finished is added by this migration, verified by grepping it for each of the five names (PRD 5).
